description: Five-panel SEM surface-morphology figure (all secondary-electron-type images) of SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni low-density steel, one panel per laser power: (a) 70, (b) 90, (c) 110, (d) 130 and (e) 150 W, per the caption. Every panel carries a black 200 µm scale bar in its lower-right corner; no magnification or accelerating voltage is printed. (a) at 70 W shows the roughest surface: many bright spherical powder particles, irregular agglomerated lumps and dark cavities, annotated with the text "Lack of fusion" and "Hole" and marked by black and white arrows pointing to unfused particles and holes. (b) at 90 W is smoother, with faint parallel melt-track striations and scattered spherical particles still flagged "Lack of fusion" by black arrows. (c) at 110 W is the smoothest, dominated by fine directional melt-track streaks, with a single yellow arrow labelled "Balling" at one small sphere. (d) at 130 W and (e) at 150 W show progressively more spherical droplets on otherwise melt-tracked surfaces, each annotated "Balling" with yellow arrows. The group demonstrates that increasing laser power removes lack-of-fusion defects and holes up to 110 W but re-introduces balling spatter at 130–150 W.

subfigures.description: SEM surface image at 70 W (per caption). Very rough, particulate surface covered by bright spherical powder particles and irregular fused lumps, with dark holes. Text annotations "Lack of fusion" and "Hole"; black and white arrows point to unfused particles and holes. Black 200 µm scale bar, lower right.

SEM surface image at 90 W (per caption). Noticeably smoother, with faint parallel melt-track striations; scattered spherical particles remain, labelled "Lack of fusion" with black arrows. Black 200 µm scale bar, lower right.

SEM surface image at 110 W (per caption). Smoothest panel: dominant fine directional melt-track streaks, little particulate debris; a single small sphere is marked by a yellow arrow labelled "Balling". Black 200 µm scale bar, lower right.

SEM surface image at 130 W (per caption). Melt-tracked surface with several distinct spherical droplets; yellow arrows and the yellow text "Balling" annotate the spheres. Black 200 µm scale bar, lower right.

SEM surface image at 150 W (per caption). Similar melt-track texture with multiple spherical droplets marked by yellow arrows and the label "Balling", plus scattered dark specks. Black 200 µm scale bar, lower right.

observations.observation: All five panels (a)-(e) carry an identical black scale bar labelled 200 µm in the lower-right corner.
Panel (a) shows the roughest surface of the group, with numerous spherical particles, irregular fused agglomerates and dark cavities.
Panel (a) is annotated with the printed text "Lack of fusion" and "Hole", with black and white arrows pointing to unfused particles and holes.
Panel (b) is annotated "Lack of fusion" with black arrows pointing at spherical particles, on a surface showing faint parallel melt-track striations.
Panel (c) is annotated with the yellow text "Balling" and a single yellow arrow pointing at one small sphere on an otherwise smooth, melt-tracked surface.
Panels (d) and (e) both carry the yellow label "Balling" with multiple yellow arrows pointing at spherical droplets, which are more numerous than in (c).
The caption states panels (a)-(e) correspond to laser powers of 70, 90, 110, 130 and 150 W respectively for the Fe-30Mn-9Al-C-3Ni alloy.
The citing text states that numerous unfused powder particles and pores were observed at 70 W (panel a) and gradually decreased in number as laser power increased.
The citing text states the P-110 sample (110 W) exhibited the best surface quality, being devoid of any obvious unfused powder particles or pores.
The citing text attributes the improvement at 110 W to a higher laser power enlarging the melt pool, which benefits metal fusion.
The citing text states that small spheres were increasingly generated at 130 and 150 W (panels d and e) owing to localized heat accumulation.

The citing text describes panel (c) as devoid of obvious unfused powder particles or pores, yet the panel itself does show and label one small sphere as "Balling" — the visual content is slightly stronger than the citation wording.

unreadable_items: No magnification or accelerating voltage is printed on any panel; the SEM imaging conditions cannot be recovered from the figure.
